stories.headline: Marcos state visit to Japan yields comprehensive strategic partnership, GSOMIA launch, and $3.4B in investment pledges
stories.summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. completed a four-day state visit to Japan (May 27–29), during which Emperor Naruhito hosted an imperial state banquet and Prime Minister Takaichi elevated bilateral relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two sides agreed to begin GSOMIA (intelligence-sharing) negotiations, accelerate talks on transferring Abukuma-class destroyers, and expand economic cooperation including oil stockpiling under the POWERR Asia framework; Prince Hisahito made his state-banquet debut at the Imperial Palace event.

stories.headline: Defense Minister Koizumi rejects 'new militarism' accusation, criticizes China's opaque military buildup at Shangri-La Dialogue
stories.summary: At the annual Shangri-La Dialogue security conference in Singapore on May 31, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi delivered a keynote defending Japan's defense buildup as transparent and lawful, pushing back against China's 'new militarism' characterization and citing China's own rapid, opaque military expansion; Koizumi also met bilaterally with South Korean and US counterparts. stories.headline: Takaichi's $19 billion supplementary budget triggers bond market alarm; food tax cut timeline remains uncertain
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi unveiled a ¥2.9 trillion ($19 billion) supplementary budget on May 25 to subsidize fuel costs and address cost-of-living pressures, reversing earlier statements ruling out extra spending; the announcement—financed partly through deficit-covering bonds—sparked a surge in Japanese government bond yields to 40-year highs and renewed investor concern about fiscal discipline, even as the LDP separately proposed 'bridging bonds' for a 17-sector investment agenda and the government debated a phased food consumption tax cut starting April 2027.

stories.summary: Japan's latest census revealed a record 2.5% decline in population over five years, with births falling for the tenth consecutive year and all prefectures except Tokyo and Okinawa recording drops; coverage noted the irony that Prime Minister Takaichi's government is pursuing tighter immigration controls rather than increased inflows as a demographic remedy.
